claims.statement:
Measured. These corners are symmetric in schedule and decoder class. Like hw_tr, each one switches off every channel but one, so they are diagnostics of single channels, not device models.
- hw_g: XYZ^2 ties the honeycomb for third. It is 0.78 of CSS (5.0 sigma) and 0.79 of XZZX (7.4 sigma), with stat plus syst errors.
- hw_g1q: XYZ^2 is third.
- hw_t: 0.35 of CSS and 0.13 of XZZX. XYZ^2's entry is corr_gauge Y, 1.330(14)% after inflating by sqrt(chi2). Its Y-basis BM was excluded by the drift rule (pair crossing 1.617(176), drift 0.73). That rule flags only downward drift, while competitor fits drifting upward 2.0-2.5x are kept. With XYZ^2 BM the ratios would be about 0.42 and 0.16. The verdict is unchanged.

hw_t is harsher than Hetenyi-Wootton's placement. hw_tr puts idling where they do (C21, C35).

Their ordering XYZ^2 > XZZX at the gate corner (0.465 vs 0.37) is not reproduced.
- hw_g1q cannot test it: the same single-qubit error on every code keeps CSS and XZZX isomorphic.
- Their XZZX carries extra data-qubit basis changes. Their XYZ^2 also has X and Y basis conversions, which 'contribute significantly', and plaquette SWAPs. So the cause of their ordering is not isolated.

Absolute corner values differ from theirs by factors of 0.32-3.76 with best decoders and 0.21-3.11 with MWPM. The surface codes' hw_g crossings drift up more than XYZ^2's, so the hw_g gap may be understated.

claims.statement:
Threshold, measured: a tie (stat plus syst errors).
- XYZ^2's 10.63(46)% (X basis, corr_gauge) against CSS 10.50(56)% and XZZX 10.32(44)% (z 0.2 and 0.5).
- Only MWPM has fss fits in both of XYZ^2's bases. There XYZ^2 is 8% higher (10.60(28) vs 9.78(41) and 9.85(26); 1.6 and 2.0 sigma). The Y-basis MWPM fss (10.85(22)) lies above X.
- With corr_gauge and BM, XYZ^2's Y basis has only drift-flagged pair crossings (10.27(54), 9.95(82)). Its X-basis BM (10.32(119)) is level with CSS and XZZX.

Below threshold at equal qubits (pilot, repo layout: 4d^2-1 vs 2d^2-1): a loss by C33's rule. The rule needs 3 sigma under all three of its error models, with z = |ln R|/sigma: (a) Poisson; (b) f = 1.7 on each single run; (c) an extra log-rate offset delta on each XYZ^2 BM run, with delta in C33's bracket of about 0.065-0.37 and labels taken at the top, 0.37. delta* is the largest delta at which (c) still gives z = 3. Runs with other decoders are outside (c). Taking labels at the top of the bracket discounts BM losses as well as BM leads. Ratio errors are binomial stat.
- hw_rr never corrupts the data, so every logical error is a failure of the final data readout (the time boundary), and p_L does not grow with r. The probe therefore compares p_L per run (XYZ^2 d = 5, r = 15; XZZX d = 7, r = 21), not an error per round.
- The loss rests on runs outside (c). XYZ^2's weaker basis (Y) has 2.09(1)x XZZX's p_L with MWPM on both sides (z 104 and 61) and 2.10(2)x with corr_gauge against XZZX corr (z 75 and 44). Both hold. The two XYZ^2 runs are independent and agree within 0.3 sigma.
- BM, XYZ^2's best decoder here, lowers its Y-basis p_L by only 6(3)% relative to corr_gauge. Against XZZX corr the ratio is 1.98(7)x (z 19.8 and 11.6; delta* 0.225). This single BM run is delta-dependent: it holds at C33's lower estimate of delta (z 9.3 at 0.065) but not at 0.37 (z 1.8).
- XYZ^2's X basis alone is 1.36(1)x worse with MWPM on both sides (z 41 and 24). With BM against corr it is 1.31(6)x (z 6.3 and 3.7; delta* 0.079), also delta-dependent.
- CSS matches XZZX (1.00(1)x and 0.99(1)x, MWPM).
- In Hetenyi-Wootton's spin layout (4d^2 vs 3d^2), XYZ^2 d = 5 has 100 qubits, between XZZX d = 5 (75) and d = 6 (108). Against XZZX d = 5 with MWPM, XYZ^2's Y basis has 1.156(6)x the p_L (z 29 and 17), so XYZ^2 loses there with 25 more qubits. Its X basis alone is 0.755(4)x. XZZX d = 6 was not run.

hw_rr omits their readout-pair two-qubit error and reset error. Their own readout-corner lead (16.5 vs 14.5, 14%) is 0.9 times their combined RMS relative plane-fit deviations (0.12 and 0.08).

claims.regime: Combined Hetenyi-Wootton spin-qubit noise at equal rates (p_G = p_T = p_RR), or with p_G at least about 0.6 of p_T = p_RR. Threshold inferred with their combination rule (1/p = sum 1/p_i) from the repo's hw_g and hw_rr best-decoder fits (r = d, d = 11-21, honeycomb 12-20) and the hw_tr corner (idling only during ancilla readout and reset; MWPM r = d pair crossings, d <= 9), plus their fitted threshold planes. hw_tr alone is an input with no verdict of its own: an MWPM tie (stat plus syst), untested with the best decoder.
claims.statement:
Scope. The verdict covers combined spin-qubit noise at equal rates (p_G = p_T = p_RR) and mixtures with p_G at least about 0.6 of p_T = p_RR. It is an inference from the corners. The repository has no combined-noise simulation: docs/data/campaign/hw/summary.csv has only hw_g, hw_g1q, hw_t and hw_rr rows. The hw_tr corner alone is an input. Its own threshold ranking is a tie with MWPM (stat plus syst) and untested with the best decoder. Readout-weighted mixtures with less gate noise are not covered.

hw_tr corner alone (measured; pilot pair crossings; MWPM only, r = d, d <= 9; docs/data/campaign/hw/diag_hw_tr_centers.csv, 7/9 pair, fit errors):
- XZZX Z: 18.95(160)%
- XYZ^2 X: 10.49(55)%
- CSS X: 6.64(21)%
- honeycomb (4/8): 1.24-1.36%
With MWPM, XZZX-Z is above XYZ^2-X by 5.0 sigma (stat only). Each crossing rises from the 5/7 to the 7/9 pair (XZZX Z 14.26(100) to 18.95(160); XYZ^2 X 9.58(54) to 10.49(55)). Counting each code's shift as a systematic error, the gap is 1.7 sigma (stat plus syst), a tie. Rules 3.1 and 3.2 of docs/fair_comparison.md (finite-size fits over d >= 11, each code with its best decoder) do not count this gap as a threshold loss. The shifts range from about 1.2 sigma (XYZ^2 X) to 3.3 sigma (CSS X), stat only. Both pairs share the d = 7 data, so these shift figures are approximate.

Repository entry for XZZX-X. diag_hw_tr_centers.csv reports no crossing in [0.5%, 44%]. In the file's own points (docs/data/campaign/hw/points_diag.csv), d = 9 is below d = 7 up to p = 0.19 (-1.5 sigma there, stat only). It is at or above d = 7 at 8 of 9 grid points from p = 0.313 to 0.44 (+2.5 sigma at 0.313). At those rates every distance has p_L between 0.41 and 0.52, close to the 0.5 saturation, so the sign change may be a saturation effect rather than a crossing. The XZZX-X threshold location is unresolved. CSS-Z shows no crossing: d = 9 is never above d = 7 up to p = 0.44, and it is strictly lower from p = 0.30 (below that, both have 0 or 1 errors in 20,000 shots).

MWPM handicaps XYZ^2 specifically. No BM, corr or corr_gauge hw_tr threshold exists for any code. At p_T = 4% (99/97 qubits, r = 3d), XYZ^2 MWPM is 18.6(24)x (X) and 37.6(57)x (Y) worse per round than XYZ^2 BM. XZZX MWPM is 1.07(1)x (X) and 1.09(1)x (Z) its corr (unarchived pilots). In phen_b10, a 9.5-12x MWPM/BM gap at p = 2% goes with a 1.77x best/MWPM threshold gain (docs/data/campaign/thresholds.csv, r = d: bp_full 5.539(54)% vs mwpm 3.135(39)%). The same gain would put XYZ^2 at 18.5%, level with XZZX-Z. The hw_tr handicap is larger than phen_b10's. At p_T = 6%, XYZ^2 BM has Lambda(5 to 7) of 6.6(14) (X) and 6.5(13) (Y), against 3.38(2) for XZZX corr. Both allow a higher XYZ^2 value. Lambda also depends on how the effective distance grows with d, so neither figure fixes the threshold (inference). The best-decoder hw_tr ranking is untested.

Combined noise (inference). Hetenyi-Wootton's combination rule at equal rates (1/p = sum 1/p_i; 2306.17786 lines 568-576) is applied to the repo's corners: hw_g and hw_rr with the best decoder (stat plus syst), hw_tr from the MWPM 7/9 crossing (fit errors), weaker basis throughout. It gives XYZ^2 0.909(26)%, CSS 1.042(28)%, XZZX 1.150(13)% and honeycomb 0.432(3)%. XYZ^2 is 0.79 of XZZX, 8.5 sigma below it and 3.5 sigma below CSS. The loss to XZZX does not depend on XYZ^2's hw_tr term: with no hw_tr term at all, XYZ^2 reaches 0.995(30)%, still 4.7 sigma below XZZX. That bound stays at least 3 sigma below XZZX for any XZZX hw_tr threshold of 10.0% or more. XZZX's 5/7 crossing, 14.26(100)%, gives 4.1 sigma. The loss to CSS does depend on XYZ^2's hw_tr term: the bound without it is 1.1 sigma below CSS, a tie. The bound needs gate noise. With p_G = 0.5 p_T = 0.5 p_RR it is 2.4 sigma below XZZX, and with 0.3 it is 0.2 sigma below.

Basis of the combined verdict. It carries the measured hw_g loss (C19): XYZ^2 1.097(37)% against XZZX 1.389(14)% and CSS 1.400(49)%, 7.4 and 5.0 sigma below (stat plus syst). At equal rates the gate term is 83% of XYZ^2's sum of inverse thresholds, and the combined ratio to XZZX, 0.79, equals the hw_g ratio. The verdict also needs the planar rule to hold for these circuits. Hetenyi-Wootton state that the threshold surface is not a plane. Their fitted planes deviate from the surfaces by 0.11 (XZZX) and 0.12 (XYZ2) RMS relative (Table I), which is about the size of the 0.86 ratio of the no-hw_tr bound to XZZX. The rule here passes through the measured corners and the equal-rate point lies near the gate corner, so the deviation there may be smaller (inference).

Threshold planes (inference). Hetenyi-Wootton's fitted planes (ZZ links; 2306.17786 Table I) put XYZ^2 above both CSS and XZZX only near the readout corner (p_G below about 1.1% of p_RR and p_T below about 13% of p_RR), by at most 1.14x (16.5% vs 14.5%). If the RMS plane deviations (0.12 XYZ2, 0.08 surface code, 0.11 XZZX) are 1-sigma errors on each intercept, the 1.14x lead is about 0.9 sigma, a tie. That reading is an assumption: the paper says only that the deviation estimates the error of the linear approximation. The repo's readout corner is also a tie (measured): hw_rr best-decoder thresholds are XYZ^2 10.63(46)%, CSS 10.50(56)% and XZZX 10.32(44)% (stat plus syst), 0.2 and 0.5 sigma apart. Their slow-readout scenario names XZZX as the usable code.

Their 4.2% XYZ^2 idling threshold. ZZ links make Z-biased idling the Hadamard image of 2112.06036's X-bias case. Two readout windows per cycle double the idling to 8.4%, close to hw_tr's 10.5(6)% (MWPM) with XX links. So the window count may set their threshold, and link orientation may set below-threshold scaling (inference).

Verdict basis. In the hw_tr corner alone, the rules give no threshold verdict. With MWPM, XYZ^2 trails XZZX-Z by 5.0 sigma (stat only) and 1.7 sigma (stat plus syst), and the best-decoder ranking is untested. At equal rates and in gate-weighted mixtures, XYZ^2 loses to XZZX under the combination rule whatever its own hw_tr threshold. That verdict is an inference that rests on the measured hw_g loss and on the planar rule. In readout-weighted mixtures the repo's numbers do not decide, and Hetenyi-Wootton's planes give XYZ^2 at most a tie, near the readout corner. This is a threshold verdict. Below threshold in the hw_tr corner, XYZ^2 with BM has a lower error per round than XZZX at equal qubits (C35, competitive), and device-like variants remove that edge (C37, C38).

claims.regime: Gap diagnostic (SD6 variants, not hardware): noiseless links and/or no idle errors; links repeated; links as pair measurements; schedule search
claims.statement:
Measured. XYZ^2 reaches XZZX's threshold only when the link checks are noiseless and idle errors are zero; then it ties (threshold ratio 1.013(30)).

Threshold ratios, each change alone:
- noiseless links (against XZZX under SD6): 0.770(21);
- no idling (against XZZX without idling): 0.774(8).

Gap fractions (share of the gap removed). The effects are super-additive (about 3.5 sigma):
- idling 0.60(1);
- link noise 0.23(2) against XZZX without idling, or 0.43(4) against XZZX under SD6;
- both together 1.02(5).
XYZ^2 without idling against XZZX with idling gives a threshold ratio of 1.050(27). That is a cross-model comparison, not a use case.

Physical substitutes recover little (gap fractions): hybrid 0.27(3), links twice 0.22(7), links three times 0.12(3).

Schedule search:
- the best of 1690 full-distance depth-6 schedules is within statistics of the default;
- removing gate-layer idling alone raises XYZ^2's MWPM crossing from 0.38% to 0.57% (a d = 7/9 diagnostic).

sd6_noidle also removes reset and readout idling. It is a diagnostic only, not a proxy for any platform.

claims.regime: Decoder dependence: MWPM, HCM, BM/BP, sequential two-level, CFE, Tesseract, TN ML; all models, including the pilot regimes of C31 and C35
claims.statement:
Measured. With stat plus syst errors, no decoder gives XYZ^2 a win (at least 3 sigma above the best competitor) on any hardware-motivated model at any number of rounds. At r = d XYZ^2 loses on every hardware-motivated model with its best decoder, so no decoder changes a verdict there. At r < d, BP-, BM- and TN-ML-class fits turn some MWPM losses into ties (nominal ratios 0.73-0.98): SI1000 r = 1, 2, 5; si1000_lr2 r = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10; H2 without crosstalk r = 3 (bp_corr ties at 2.98 sigma, BM loses at 7.3 sigma). Both of XYZ^2's idealized edges exist only with BM/BP decoding.

Decoder gains at r = d (docs/data/campaign/competitors_table.csv; significances use stat plus syst errors from docs/data/campaign/thresholds.csv):
- XYZ^2's best/MWPM is 1.16-1.90, against 1.01-1.18 for XZZX. XY gains as much under bias (1.71-1.82).
- XYZ^2's best decoder against every competitor on MWPM: loses under SD6 (0.73, 16 sigma), bias (0.42-0.68, at least 11 sigma) and H2 without crosstalk (0.87, 3.5 sigma). Under Helios without crosstalk (0.83) it loses by 12 sigma with BM 0.407(3)% and ties at 2.3 sigma with the bp_corr fit 0.408(35)%, whose syst error is large. It ties under SI1000 (0.98) and phen_b10 (1.01) and leads under phen (1.09, 5.4 sigma, not hardware).

r = 1 preparation:
- In the MDR basis (depth-6 L_X), the better of TN ML and CFE-TN gains 1.01-1.10x over MWPM across eight models (SD6 1.08x).
- XYZ^2 loses at r = 1 in every hardware-motivated model except SI1000 and si1000_lr2 (C3) and H2 with crosstalk (C13). Under SI1000 the depth-6 L_Y TN ML fit 1.059(91)% ties CSS bm 1.078(59)% (0.2 sigma), while XYZ^2 MWPM 0.959(16)% loses to XZZX bm 1.055(23)% at 3.4 sigma.

Asymmetry in decoder coverage:
- Competitor entries use only bm, corr and mwpm at fss.
- XYZ^2's head-to-head entry uses a decoder no competitor has at fss in 87 of 107 rows. It is 86 if Tesseract counts as shared and 65 if bp_full (belief-matching) also counts as BM.
- The only hardware-motivated row with a nominal XYZ^2 lead is H2 with crosstalk at r = 5: Tesseract, L_X only, 0.817(17)% against XZZX bm 0.578(102)%, ratio 1.41. That is a tie at 2.3 sigma with stat plus syst and 12.5 sigma with stat only. XYZ^2's BM fit there is 0.420(3)%.
- Competitor BP-OSD and Tesseract exist only as pair crossings (d <= 11), never as fss fits. Their non-drift d = 9/11 single-basis crossings fall on both sides of the same code's fss values. Admitted into the selection rules of paper/analysis/competitor_report.py, they raise no best-competitor entry at r = d in the models without crosstalk. They raise it in 12 non-crosstalk (model, r) rows at r = 1-10. Pair-crossing errors below are stat only; fss entry errors are stat plus syst. The largest changes: purez r = 10 XZZX-Z Tesseract 4.24(63)% against corr 2.41(8)%, ratio from 0.47 to 0.26; phen r = 1 XZZX-Z Tesseract 17.08(138)% against bm 15.72(38)%, ratio from 1.08 to 0.99; phen_b10 r = 5 XZZX-X BP-OSD 10.76(124)% against bm 9.62(50)%, ratio from 0.78 to 0.70 (still a tie at 2.3 sigma); phen r = 5 CSS-Z BP-OSD 7.26(81)% against 6.96(24)%, ratio from 0.93 to 0.89; biased100 r = 10 from 2.18% to 2.32%, ratio from 0.47 to 0.44. Under H2 with crosstalk the entry rises at r = 1 to XZZX-Z BP-OSD 1.956(130)% (ratio from 0.83 to 0.59, which turns the tie at 1.7 sigma into a loss at 4.7 sigma), at r = 5 to XZZX-X BP-OSD 0.904(106)% (ratio from 1.41 to 0.90), at r = 10 to CSS-X BP-OSD 0.595(25)% (ratio from 0.64 to 0.53) and at r = d to CSS-X Tesseract 0.450(25)% (ratio from 0.77 to 0.69). Every change lowers XYZ^2's ratio. Competitor BP-OSD and Tesseract fss fits are untested.

Equal qubits (docs/data/campaign/eq/pairs.csv and points_eps.csv, r = 3d):
- Against CSS under bias: 3.5-58x better (corr) to 1.7-9.3x worse (MWPM).
- Against XZZX: 10-850x worse with corr, 61-72,000x worse with MWPM.
- BM narrows the XZZX gap to 3.4-6.9x at 99/97 qubits (weaker basis), but not at 323/337: 28x (biased100) and 51x (purez) at p = 3e-3. Those two XYZ^2 BM points are L_X only with 16 errors each (about 25% stat error).

The idealized edges with matching-class decoders:
- phen_b10 (p = 2%, 50/49 data qubits; XYZ^2 L_X against XZZX's weaker basis X): corr_gauge 3.03e-4 (4,495 errors) against XZZX corr 1.875e-4 (7,738 errors), 1.62(3)x worse. MWPM against MWPM: 1.797e-3 (81,809 errors) against 2.357e-4 (10,999 errors), 7.62(8)x worse.
- hw_tr (p_T 4%, 99/97): XYZ^2 corr_gauge in its worse basis Y is 6.92e-4 (16,684 errors) in an unarchived probe and 7.07e-4 (15,023 errors) in an unarchived rerun of docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/rv/eqprobe.py, against XZZX corr 3.050e-4 (11,782 errors): 2.27(3)-2.32(3)x worse. XYZ^2 MWPM Y 4.58e-3 (unarchived probe) is 15x XZZX corr. No XZZX MWPM point at this p_T is archived; an unarchived XZZX MWPM run gives 3.29e-4 (16,096 errors), about 14x MWPM against MWPM.
- This matches arXiv:2505.03691: matching-class XYZ^2 decoding gains nothing from eta = 10 bias (code capacity 18.4% against 18.3% depolarizing; phenomenological 3.49% against 3.42%), while BM (24.1%, 4.30%) and ML (28.6%) exploit it.

Cost in this repository's Python implementation (docs/data/campaign/eq/timing.csv): BM takes 0.11-0.48 s per shot at d = 11-15 (XYZ^2 0.33-0.36 s at d = 11), against 5.5e-5 to 1.7e-3 s for corr and corr_gauge. No optimized BP-class decoder was timed, so whether BM can run in real time is untested. Hetenyi-Wootton call real-time decoding a requirement.

claims.regime: Fairness and selection effects of the comparison rules
claims.statement:
Measured. Across all rows the rules favour XYZ^2 (a median effect), and it still never wins. Under the symmetric rules below (thresholds.csv errors, stat plus syst) XYZ^2 loses in 82 of 97 rows and ties in 15. Under the table rule it loses in 85 of 107 rows and ties in 22.

Favouring XYZ^2:
- Its entry is the maximum over about 20 usable schedule-decoder fits of its weaker basis (16-27, median 21, in the 96 non-crosstalk rows). The competitors get at most 12 (6-12, usually 12; 20-24 under hyb).
- A decoder that no competitor gets at fss is used in 86-87 of 107 rows (C23). Rule 3.2 gives XYZ^2 every decoder of TwoLevelDecoder. It also gives the surface codes BP-OSD and Tesseract, but those ran only to d = 11 and have only pair crossings, with no fss fit, so the table never uses them.
- Admitting the competitors' d = 9/11 BP-OSD and Tesseract pair crossings (stat errors only, not flagged drift) raises the best-competitor entry in 12 non-crosstalk base-model rows at r = 1-10 (18 counting the sd6_lr2, sd6_lr3 and sd6_il rows that inherit sd6) and in none at r = d. phen r = 1 falls from 1.08 to 0.99 (XZZX-Z Tesseract 17.08(138)% against 15.72(38)%), phen_b10 r = 5 from 0.78 to 0.70 (XZZX-X BP-OSD 10.76(124)%), phen r = 5 from 0.93 to 0.89 and biased100 r = 10 from 0.47 to 0.44. Below the top competitor, the XY-X BP-OSD crossing at biased100 r = 10, 1.268(102)%, would replace XY's MWPM entry 0.843(16)%. That turns XYZ^2's 3.9-sigma lead over XY (1.029(45)%) into a 2.1-sigma deficit (C5, C27). Some crossings drift upward (purez r = 10: XZZX-Z Tesseract 4.24(63)% against the fss entry 2.41(8)%), so they show that competitor fss values are missing but do not measure them.
- Where XYZ^2's weaker basis has no usable fit, the table keeps its stronger basis and marks it 'only'. A competitor code without usable fits in both bases is dropped instead. Six crosstalk rows are set this way (helios_p r = 1, 3; h2_p r = 1, 2, 3, 5), and in each of them the other basis was run. At h2_p r = 5 the entry is depth6 L_X Tesseract 0.817(17)%, while the depth6 L_Y pair crossings are 0.155-0.321% (corr_gauge 0.255(23)%). That entry produces the nominal ratio 1.41 (C13, C27).
- Measured effect: the table entry exceeds the symmetric value by up to 12.7% (purez r = 3). The excess is above 10% also at purez r = 10, hyb_lr2 r = 1, em3 r = 1 and si1000 r = 1. The median excess over 97 rows is 2.5%, and at r = d it is at most 5.2% (sd6).
- Winner's curse: the maximum tends to pick higher or noisier fits, which turns losses into ties. With stat plus syst errors, h2_p_noxt r = 3 is 1.147(127)% in the table and 1.108(20)% with matched decoders, z -2.98 and -7.35 (C2). Six non-crosstalk table ties are losses under the symmetric rules: h2_p_noxt r = 3; si1000 r = 1 (0.959(16)% against XZZX-Z BM 1.055(23)%, z -3.4); si1000 r = 5 (0.622(15)% against XZZX-X corr 0.705(12)%, z -4.4); phen_b10 r = 5 (7.257(148)% against XZZX-Z BM 9.617(496)%, z -4.6); and the sd6_il diagnostic at r = 5 (table 1.048(70)%, z -2.8; symmetric 1.007(25)%, z -4.8) and at r = 10 (0.901(96)%, z -2.0; 0.845(30)%, z -6.0). si1000 r = 3 moves the other way, from a table loss (z -3.4) to a tie (z -2.1).
- XYZ^2 may use depth6 L_Y, whose fault distance is (d+1)/2. The hyb rule refuses the surface codes' direct compilation for that same reason, and the third hybrid option in section 2 was never built.
- BOTH_BASES_SCHEDULE was selected on SD6 MWPM error and is then compared under SD6.
- Native degree-6 connectivity is assumed, with no routing cost.

Favouring the competitors:
- The maximum over CSS, XZZX and XY. These are replicates only where they agree within errors: sd6, si1000, phen and em3 (inverse-variance chi2 at most 3.1 over the three codes). There the maximum is at most 1.0% above the pooled value at r = d, and up to 5.3% at sd6 r = 5 (4.4% at r = 3). Under the ion and biased models the three differ (chi2 306 at helios_p_noxt r = d, 1166 at biased10 r = d), so the maximum is a choice of best code. The symmetric rules keep this maximum. Pooling the three codes' table entries (inverse-variance) instead changes no win, tie or loss label.
- Per-ancilla crosstalk at equal d.
- The equal-qubit campaign uses correlated matching (corr_gauge) for XYZ^2. Under biased100 and purez its BM error is 1.5-6.8x lower (median 2.3x, 40 points with at least 30 errors for each decoder). In XZZX's weaker basis there (X, at 45 of 49 points), BM changes the error by a factor 0.72-1.27. The BM results are reported separately.

Either direction:
- The drift rule flags only downward drift. This goes against XYZ^2 in hw_t (C19). The rule keeps upward-drifting fits, among them the purez r = 10 XZZX-Z BM fit (drift 2.07) and corr fit (drift 1.48), whose values 2.18(18)% and 2.41(8)% lie below their last crossings, 3.18% and 2.84%.
- In 6 of the 24 replicate rows the competitor replicate excess is larger than XYZ^2's table excess (sd6 r = 5: 5.3% against 3.6%; si1000 r = d, 2, 3 and 10; phen r = 10). 'The rules favour XYZ^2' is therefore a statement about the median, not about every row.

Not asymmetries: the SD6 idle convention (rule 1, 'a code whose rounds take more steps pays for them'), about 60% of the gap.

Symmetric rules (both schedule; mwpm/corr_gauge/bm against mwpm/corr/bm; same competitor entries as the table), reproducible from /pscratch/sd/s/sohan100/XYZ-2-MDR-Logical-State-Preparation/docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/fairrev/sym.py:
- r = d: sd6 0.60, si1000 0.83, biased10/100/purez 0.62/0.49/0.41, helios/h2_noxt 0.76/0.75, phen 0.89, phen_b10 0.98, em3 0.16 against the honeycomb (1.27-1.30 against the pair-measurement surface codes).
- r = 1: si1000 0.89, phen 1.01, hyb_lr2 0.855 against the gate surface codes (0.59 against the honeycomb).
- The 15 ties: phen r = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10; phen_b10 r = d, 10; si1000 r = 2, 3; si1000_lr2 r = 1, 2, 3, 5, 10; sd6_il r = 2. Two have ratios above 1: phen r = 1 at 1.009 (z +0.2) and phen_b10 r = 10 at 1.038 (z +0.6). None is a win.

The hw corners and rule 1. Every Hetenyi-Wootton corner (hw_g, hw_g1q, hw_t, hw_rr, hw_tr) runs with all other channels noiseless. 'Nothing is noiseless' therefore does not single out hw_tr; fair_comparison.md section 3.4 names only sd6_il.

What distinguishes hw_tr is that it waives gate-layer idling, which costs XYZ^2 about 4.9x more (254 against 52 sites per round). Rule 1's third bullet says a code with more steps must pay that cost. In the m1 mixture of C37 (hw_tr plus gate and readout error), applying 2% of p_T on gate-layer idle sites gives 1.02(7), so no edge is seen there. The change from m1's nominal 0.70(4) is a trend, not established (C37).

claims.regime: Noise that lacks the link Pauli: (a) Z-biased dephasing in the XX-link frame (tested; C35, C37); (b) amplitude-damping idle noise (p_X = p_Y >> p_Z) with ZZ links (untested)
claims.statement:
Case (a), measured in pilots. Each ratio is XYZ^2 BM in its weaker basis over square XZZX corr in its weaker basis, at 99/97 qubits, r = 3d and eta = 20 unless stated. Brackets are Poisson errors. Significances are stat only and use C33's form z = |ln R|/sigma, quoted as (a)/(b)/(c) for C33's three error models: (a) Poisson; (b) XYZ^2's Poisson error scaled by its own replicate scatter (1.7 for a single run), read as Student t when the scale exceeds 1; (c) an extra offset of delta = 0.15 and 0.25 per XYZ^2 run. A lead or loss counts only at 3 sigma under all three (C33).
- With perfect syndromes (hw_tr, C35) the XYZ^2 lead meets that rule only at r = 6d, p_T 4%: 0.38(4), z 9.5/9.5/6.5 and 4.7. At r = 3d it does not: 0.61(4) at p_T 6% (7.2/4.2/3.0 and 1.9) and 0.61(8) at p_T 4% (3.9/2.3/2.5 and 1.8).
- The lead needs BM. With corr_gauge XYZ^2 is about 2.3x worse in its weaker basis (Y) at p_T 4%, even with perfect syndromes (stat error 0.03 per run). With MWPM it is about 15x worse (C35). The other decoders (bp_corr, CFE, Tesseract, the TN decoders) were not run under hw_tr.
- With 0.1% gates and 1% readout (m1, p_T 4%, f = 0) a nominal lead remains: 0.70(4), z 5.7/2.0/3.6 and 2.5. Model (b) is t = 3.44 on 3 dof from the scatter of four replicates (scale 1.66). C33 rates m1 not established. At 195 qubits m1 gives 0.81(17), z 1.0 under (a), a tie. With 0.3% gates (one run) it is 0.75(6), z 3.7/2.2/1.7 and 1.1, a tie.
- Gate-layer dephasing was run only at f = 0, 0.02 and 0.05 of p_T. At f = 0.02 the ratio is 1.02(7) and at f = 0.05 it is 1.27(12) (z 0.3 and 2.7 under (a)), so neither shows a lead (C37). 0 < f < 0.02 is untested.
- With Z-biased error at the full rate p on every gate, idle, reset and measurement location (purez, biased100, p = 1e-3 to 3e-3), XYZ^2 BM loses at every equal-qubit pair with at least 16 XYZ^2 errors: 3.4-6.9x in its weaker basis at 99/97, and 28x and 51x in L_X at 323/337 (p = 3e-3; Y not run). Each loss is at least 4.7 sigma under all three models (C6).
So, among the tested settings, a nominal XYZ^2 lead appears only with BM and only at f = 0, and it meets C33's rule only with perfect syndromes at r = 6d. BM with f = 0 is not sufficient. At p_T 1.5% with 2.7% readout (0.1% gates, f = 0, run E) XYZ^2 is worse: 1.72(16), z 5.7/5.7/3.8 and 2.7, a loss for delta up to 0.22. Readout and p_T are confounded in that run (C37). At p_T 3% with perfect syndromes no tested bias gives a lead that meets the rule: eta = 10, 20 and 100 give 0.81(8), 0.68(8) and 1.14(19). Only eta = 20 reaches 3 sigma under (a), at 3.3, and it is 2.4 under (c) at delta 0.15 (C35).

Case (b), untested.
- The inner [[2,1,1]] link detects both non-link Paulis.
- 2505.03691 suggests exploring -ZZ links tailored to relaxation; it does not propose them.

Inference about platforms: T1-limited idling occurs mainly on superconducting qubits, which lack degree-6 couplers. For spins T2 << T1. In neutral atoms, atom loss is a dominant error source (2603.24237).

claims.regime: Phenomenological noise with Z bias eta = 10 (phen_b10; readout flips at q = p on weight-6 and weight-2 checks alike; not hardware). Equal qubit count below threshold, memory at r = 3d, p = 1.5-3%. Pooled pilots in docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/ (bq, ul, stat, ovc); sizes are data qubits
claims.statement:
Measured in pooled pilots, not campaign standard. The setting is memory at r = 3d. XYZ^2 BM in its weaker basis is compared with square XZZX in its distance-d frame, decoded with corr, which is XZZX's lower-error decoder at d = 4 and 7. Ratios R are XYZ^2/XZZX with Poisson errors. All errors are statistical; no systematic error is included. Significance follows C33 item 4 in log form, z = |ln R|/sigma, under three error models: (a) Poisson; (b) shot-level scaling, with f = max(1, sqrt(chi2/dof)) from a pool's own replicates and f = 1.7 for a single run, on either side, and with z read as Student t on k - 1 dof where f > 1 is estimated from k replicates; (c) an extra log-rate variance delta^2 per XYZ^2 BM run, with competitor runs Poisson. delta* is the largest delta at which (c) still gives z = 3. C33 puts delta at about 0.065-0.37: 0.065 over all 42 replicate sets (0.074 over the 35 XYZ^2 BM sets), a lower estimate, and 0.165-0.374 for the four flagged sets. Labels follow C33 item 4. A lead or loss holds if z is at least 3 under (a) and (b) and delta* is at least 0.37. A point that passes (a) and (b) with delta* between 0.065 and 0.37 is delta-dependent and is not counted. A point that fails (a) or (b) is a tie. Rows give R, z under (a) and (b), and delta*.

Nominal XYZ^2 leads:
- 18/16 data qubits, p = 3%, one run per side, against XZZX d = 4 (even distance): 0.70(5); z 5.3, 3.1; delta* 0.097, delta-dependent. Against XZZX interpolated log-linearly in qubit number between d = 4 (corr) and d = 5 (BM; no d = 5 corr run): 0.78(5); z 4.0, 2.4, a tie.
- 50/49, p = 3%, L_X, the worse basis (two runs, chi2 0.40 on 1): 0.81(4); z 4.8, 4.7; delta* 0.078, delta-dependent.
- 50/49, p = 2.5%, L_X, the worse basis (two runs, chi2 0.27 on 1): 0.78(5); z 3.7, 3.7; delta* 0.069, delta-dependent.
- 50/49, p = 2%, L_Y, the worse basis (eight runs, chi2 4.16 on 7): 0.81(4); z 4.1, 4.1; delta* 0.133, delta-dependent. L_X (ten runs, chi2 21.1 on 9, f = 1.53): 0.78(4); z 5.3, 2.7 (Student t on 9 dof); delta* 0.211. It fails (b) and is a tie. The L_X scatter comes from the two stat/ runs, which give 1.03(9) together; the other eight give 0.72(4) (chi2 9.6 on 7).
Under (a) and (b) the lead reaches 3 sigma at two sizes: 18/16 against XZZX d = 4, and 50/49 at p = 2% (L_Y), 2.5% and 3%. These four points have delta* 0.069-0.133, inside C33's bracket, so they are delta-dependent leads and are not counted. At delta = 0.065 all four would hold, at 0.074 all but 2.5% would, and at 0.37 none does. No lead is established, and whether these leads count depends on delta. The same rule leaves the q = 0 L_Y loss delta-dependent (delta* 0.213).

Points that do not resolve the trend in size or p. Each lies within 3 sigma of 1 and of 0.81 under (a):
- 98/100, p = 3%: L_X 0.91(8) (six runs). With XZZX BM at d = 10 (23 errors) as the comparator it is 1.19(26).
- 98/100, p = 2.5%: L_Y, the worse basis, 0.88(13), against XZZX corr interpolated between d = 9 and d = 11.
- 98/100, p = 2%: L_Y 0.94(23) (18 errors).
- 50/49, p = 1.5%: L_X, the worse basis, 1.06(12) from six logs (82 errors, chi2 4.54 on 5). Four of these logs (stat/run15_*) stopped at 48 s and have no parameter line. Their naming, output format and error rate match d = 5 at p = 1.5% (inference). The two complete logs alone give 0.99(16) (37 errors). This point lies 2.2 sigma above the p = 2% L_Y ratio, so the lead may shrink at lower p. Neither fading nor persistence is established.
- Size trend: XYZ^2 Lambda (d = 5 to 7, p = 3%) is 3.8(3). XZZX corr gives 4.29(20) or 4.10(24) over the same sizes, 1.3 and 0.8 sigma away.

Scope: the nominal lead is a memory result. At r = 1 (single-round MDR preparation, C10), p = 3%, 50/49, the archived pilot gives XYZ^2 BM L_X 1.446(86)e-3 (284 errors) against XZZX corr L_X, XZZX's weaker basis, 1.717(52)e-4 (1080 errors). XYZ^2 is 8.4(6)x worse; z 32, 19; delta* 0.71. This loss holds under C33's rule. Unarchived repeat runs of the same script give 9.8-11.2x against XZZX L_X in C10's runs and 9.9(5)x in a further run, up to 14.1x against XZZX L_Z (C10), and 15.1(7)x in L_Y, XYZ^2's weaker basis in those runs. This fits the r = 1 threshold gap in C9 and C17.

Dependence on decoder and readout:
- The lead needs BP-class decoders. bp_full replicates agree with BM. At p = 2%, 50/49, L_X, XYZ^2 corr_gauge is 1.62(3)x XZZX corr and XYZ^2 MWPM is 7.62(8)x XZZX MWPM.
- Noiseless readout (q = 0), p = 3%: 18/16 gives 0.62(4); z 7.5, 4.4; delta* 0.144, a delta-dependent lead. At 50/49 XYZ^2 BM is worse than XZZX corr in both bases. L_Y, the worse basis, is 1.44(9) (four runs, chi2 1.98 on 3); z 6.0, 4.7; delta* 0.213, a delta-dependent loss. L_X is 1.22(8) (chi2 4.73 on 3, f = 1.26); z 3.1, 1.6 (Student t on 3 dof), a tie. BP-class decoders do not bring L_Y below XZZX (bp_corr 1.56(28), bp_full 1.38(17)). A single bp_corr L_X point, 0.67(18), rests on 15 errors.
- Z bias eta = 100, p = 3%, 50/49: 0.98(9). Readout q = p/10, p = 5%, 50/49: 0.92(5).
- More readout noise helped XYZ^2 here. That may run against hw_tr at p_T 1.5% with readout 2.7% (C37), where readout and p_T are confounded.

Competitors and frames:
- The d^2 frame under Z bias was run as the XY code. Square XZZX aligned to Y differs from XY by X<->Y on half the data qubits. That map leaves phen_b10 unchanged (p_X = p_Y, noiseless checks with outcome flips), so the XY runs stand for it (inference from the circuit code). With BM and corr this code loses to both XZZX corr and XYZ^2. At p = 2%, 49 qubits, XY BM is 1.33(11)x XZZX corr, and XYZ^2 L_Y is 0.61(6)x XY BM. XY with corr does worse still. At p = 2.5%, XYZ^2 L_X is 0.59(6)x XY BM.
- At code capacity with eta = 10 and near-ML decoding (EWD for XYZ^2; MPS, the paper's stated XZZX decoder, for XZZX), 2112.06036 (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 7) finds a lower XYZ^2 failure rate than the d-frame XZZX at equal qubits under Z bias (Fig. 7a inset), the direction seen here. Under Y bias, where XZZX is in its d^2 frame, XZZX is suppressed and its failure rate scales with the number of data qubits (Fig. 7c). That means no clear XYZ^2 advantage over the d^2 frame at equal data qubits (inference from the text and figure). The XY ordering here is the reverse, which points to decoder limits rather than the frame (inference). ML-class decoding of the d^2-frame code is untested and could remove this lead.
- Rectangular, co-prime and tailored XZZX were not run.

claims.statement:
Measured in pooled pilots (not campaign standard). The replicates are homogeneous. Ratios are XYZ^2/XZZX logical error per round, so above 1 means XYZ^2 is worse.
- XYZ^2 BM in its weaker basis (Y) is 3.3-3.4x worse than XZZX d = 7 on corr in its weaker basis (X), +-8-10% (stat only). Per tick (8 vs 6 ticks per round, C25) it is about 2.5x worse.
- This is a loss under C33's pilot rule, which requires 3 sigma under all three of its error models. z is 12.9-14.7 with Poisson errors, at least 10.4 with shot-level scaling, and 10.1-10.9 with a run-level offset of delta = 0.25 (all stat only).
- With correlated matching (corr_gauge) in its weaker basis (Y), XYZ^2 is 6.4-6.7x worse (Poisson z >= 34, stat only).

At this point only BM and corr_gauge were run for XYZ^2, and corr_gauge is about 1.9x worse than BM in Y. At biased10, CFE, Tesseract and the BP variants were run only in the threshold campaign. In the both-Y schedule used by these pilots, their r = d thresholds (CFE 0.656(30)%, Tesseract 0.680(24)%, bp_corr 0.772(10)%) are not above BM's 0.765(10)%. So no measured decoder points to a large gain over BM at biased10 (inference from thresholds, not from sub-threshold rates at p = 3e-3). claims.regime: Statistical standard of the threshold comparisons and of the pilots (all models)
claims.statement:
Measured (methodology). Threshold z use stat+syst errors from docs/data/campaign/competitors.csv, the source of docs/data/campaign/competitors_table.csv, unless marked stat-only. Table files are in docs/data/campaign/. Pilot paths are relative to docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/.

1. Calibration.
- On identical SD6 detector error models the stat-only pull rms is about 0.7-1.2 and the stat+syst rms about 0.4-0.7. The fit-window syst term is common to identical models.
- Pair-crossing comparisons reach rms pulls of 1.7, and mixed fss/pair comparisons about 2.
- High-statistics fits are not inflated for misfit.
- The fss errors omit the extrapolation/drift systematic. Last-crossing ratios can differ a lot from fss ratios (e.g. biased10 r = d 0.85 vs 0.64). Across the 107 ratio rows the last-crossing ratio is higher in 48 and lower in 59 (median log ratio -0.04), so the shift has no systematic sign.
- Stat errors are bootstrap estimates. The competitor fits in thresholds.csv and competitors.csv have identical thresholds and syst terms, but their stat errors differ by a factor of 0.84-1.22 (5-95%). Stat-only labels near 3 sigma are therefore unstable.

2. Selection. XYZ^2 entries are maxima over 16-27 candidate fits (median 21) in the 96 rows without crosstalk and over 1-9 in the 11 crosstalk rows (h2_p, helios_p). Competitor entries are maxima over about 12, plus 3 isomorphic replicates in unbiased models. There is no fixed rule for pooling the replicates. Pooling the BM fits of CSS, XZZX and XY (both bases, 4-6 per row, inverse variance) was checked for the 19 ties in unbiased models and the near-tie losses phen r = d and si1000 r = 10. With independent syst it turns sd6_il r = 5 (a diagnostic) from a tie (-2.92) into a loss (-3.22), and the h2_p r = 5 artifact into a nominal win (+6.9). With the syst treated as common (item 1) neither label changes (-2.84 and +2.98). The other ties stay within 2.7 sigma. phen r = d moves from -2.8 against the best single fit to -5.8 pooled (-3.8 with a common syst), a loss either way.

3. Multiplicity and ties.
- 107 of 261 table rows are XYZ^2-vs-best comparisons, so about 2.4 one-sided false 2-sigma excursions are expected.
- 103 rows have XYZ^2 nominally lower. The 4 'xyz2' winners are phen_b10 r = d (z 0.03), phen r = 1 (1.05), h2_p r = 5 (2.30, an artifact) and phen_b10 r = 10 (1.14).
- 24 rows lie within 3 sigma of the best competitor, 4 of them with non-negative sign (all phen, phen_b10 or crosstalk). Two of the 24 are losses to another competitor: phen r = d (-4.03 against XZZX bm X) and si1000 r = 10 (-3.47 against CSS-Z bm). By the rule in item 5 the 107 rows give 0 wins, 22 ties and 85 losses. The thresholds.csv competitor errors give the same counts.
- With stat-only errors (thresholds.csv stat column), 14 of the 22 ties stay ties: phen_b10 r = d (+0.05) and r = 10 (+1.87), phen r = 1 (+1.21), si1000 r = 1 (-0.25), si1000_lr2 r = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 (-0.34 to -2.99), sd6_il r = 2 (-2.66) and phen r = 2, 3, 5 and 10 (-0.59 to -2.35). si1000_lr2 r = 5 is on the boundary: it is -3.30 with the competitors.csv stat errors.
- With stat-only errors h2_p r = 5 becomes a nominal win (+12.5), an artifact. h2_p r = 1 has no usable stat-only z, because its XYZ^2 cfe_tn fit has a stat error of about 1e-13. Over the other 17 negative ties the stat-only z spans -0.25 (si1000 r = 1) to -7.7 (h2_p_noxt r = 3).

4. Pilots.
- Replicates of identical XYZ^2 BM configurations from different runs exceed Poisson scatter at p < 0.05 in 4 of about 17 sets:
  - phen_b10 p = 2% X, 10 runs: chi2 21.1 on 9 dof (p 0.012);
  - phen_b10 d = 7 p = 3% Y, 5 runs: 11.9 on 4 (p 0.018);
  - hw_tr p_T = 3% X, 2 runs: 5.35 on 1 (p 0.021);
  - the m1 mixture at 99 qubits X, 4 runs: 8.3 on 3 (p 0.040).
- Four or more of 17 at p < 0.05 has probability 0.009 under Poisson, but the sets were grouped after inspection. The archived test over identically logged configurations (statrev/homog.py) gives chi2 80.8 on 69 dof (p 0.16).
- In three flagged sets one run or one pair of runs carries the excess. Without the two stat/ runs (66 and 62 errors), 2% X gives 9.6 on 7 dof (p 0.21). Without ul/e_phenb10_xyz2_Y_d7_p0.03_bm_29.txt (10 errors), the d = 7 Y set gives 4.0 on 3 (p 0.26). Without cons/m1_x_X_b.txt (45 errors), m1 X gives 1.2 on 2 (p 0.55). The hw_tr pair are two runs of one batch (cons/x3_X_a.txt and cons/x3_X_b.txt).
- Inference: these are run- or batch-level offsets, not uniform shot-level overdispersion. The cause is untested; seeds are time-based and unrecorded.
- Error models. For a pilot ratio R, z = |ln R|/sigma, with the same model whether XYZ^2 leads or trails:
  (a) Poisson: sigma^2 = 1/N1 + 1/N2 over the two error counts.
  (b) Uniform shot-level scaling: sigma^2 = f1^2/N1 + f2^2/N2. A pool takes f = max(1, sqrt(chi2/dof)) from its own replicates, and a single run takes f = 1.7 (m1's 1.66). Where f > 1 is estimated from k replicates, z is read as Student t on k - 1 dof and converted to a Gaussian-equivalent sigma.
  (c) Run-level offset: each XYZ^2 BM run gets an extra log-rate variance delta^2, and runs are pooled by inverse variance. A set of runs then has E[chi2] - dof = delta^2 W, with W = sum_i mu_i(1 - mu_i/E), where mu_i is the expected error count of run i and E the set's total. This estimator gives delta = 0.169, 0.284, 0.374 and 0.165 for the four flagged sets. They were selected after inspection, and 0.374 rests on one degree of freedom. Over all 42 replicate sets of statrev/homog.py the same estimator gives 0.065 (0.074 over its 35 XYZ^2 BM sets). homog.py groups only identically logged runs, so offsets between sources, such as the two stat/ runs of phen_b10 2% X, are partly excluded, and 0.065 is a lower estimate. delta therefore lies in about 0.065-0.37. delta* is the largest delta at which (c) still gives z = 3.
- Scope of (c). (c) is applied to XYZ^2 BM runs, which carry all four flagged offsets. Competitor runs keep Poisson errors. Two competitor replicate checks are Poisson-consistent: XZZX corr at phen_b10 2%, d = 7 (two runs, within 1.0 sigma) and three biased10 XZZX corr runs (chi2 2.18 on 2). One is not: the phen_b10 r = 1, p = 3% XZZX corr X runs (r1_phen_xzzx.out, 1,080 errors in 6,291,200 shots, plus unarchived runs quoted in C10 and C31) give chi2 14.0 on 4 (p 0.007) and delta 0.044. A competitor offset of 0.044 changes no label (at XYZ^2 delta 0.37: hw_tr r = 6d z 3.38, phen 98/100 3.10). Whether runs with other XYZ^2 decoders carry offsets is untested.
- Labels. A pilot lead or loss holds if z is at least 3 under (a) and (b) and delta* is at least 0.37, the top of the bracket. A pilot without XYZ^2 BM runs is outside (c) and holds on (a) and (b). A point that passes (a) and (b) with delta* between 0.065 and 0.37 is delta-dependent and is not counted. A point that fails (a) or (b) is a tie. Rows give R(Poisson error), z under (a) and (b), and delta*.
- Delta dependence. Using the top of the bracket discounts leads and losses alike, so the rule is conservative in both directions, and the number of established pilot results depends on delta. The top rests on one flagged set with one degree of freedom (hw_tr 3% X), selected after inspection. At delta 0.065-0.074, the all-set estimate, six more qubit-matched leads would hold: hw_tr 6% at r = 3d, hw_tr 6% at 195 qubits, hw_tr 3% L_Y, phen_b10 2% L_Y, phen_b10 3% L_X and phen_b10 18/16 against XZZX d = 4. All six are in the idealized hw_tr and phen_b10 models. Five more losses would also hold: run E, phen 50/49, phen_b10 q = 0 L_Y, phen 18/16 and hw_rr BM. At delta 0.15, hw_tr 6% at r = 3d (delta* 0.148) is borderline.
- Qubit-matched leads:
  - hw_tr p_T 4%, 99/97, r = 6d, worse basis against worse basis as docs/fair_comparison.md item 3 requires (cons/b_x_Y_a.txt 52 and cons/b_x_Y_b.txt 47 errors at r = 30, chi2 0.23 on 1, against cons/b_z_X.txt, XZZX d = 7 corr, 14,848 errors at r = 42): 0.384(39); 9.5, 9.4; delta* 0.43 (z 3.4 at delta 0.37). Holds. Better basis against better basis (cons/b_x_X_a.txt and cons/b_x_X_b.txt, 93 errors, against cons/b_z_Z.txt, 9,381 errors at r = 42): 0.564(59); 5.5, 5.45; delta* 0.227. Delta-dependent.
  - The worse-basis label has a narrow margin. delta* 0.43 is 16% above the bracket top. (c) also treats the two XYZ^2 runs as having independent offsets; both used time- and pid-based seeds (cons/hwtr_r.py line 21). If they shared one offset, delta* would be 0.30 and z at delta 0.37 would be 2.5. The hw_tr 3% X pair shows that two runs of one batch can differ, which supports independent offsets (inference). If offsets were per batch instead, the flagged sets that span sources give a top of 0.284, below 0.30 (inference).
  - hw_tr p_T 6%, 99/97, r = 3d (litrev/hwtr_xyz2_Y.txt, 218 errors, against litrev/hwtr_xzzx_X.txt): 0.61(4); 7.2, 4.2; delta* 0.148. Delta-dependent.
  - phen_b10 50/49, 2%, L_Y, the worse basis (8 runs in ul/, stat/, bq/p02b.log and ovc/res20.jsonl, 402 errors, chi2 4.16 on 7, against the five-run XZZX X corr pool of C31, 20,809 errors, chi2 1.39 on 4): 0.81(4); 4.1, 4.1; delta* 0.13. Delta-dependent.
  - phen_b10 50/49, 3%, L_X, the worse basis (bq/p03.log and ul/c_xyz2_X_d5_p0.03_bm_5.txt, 514 errors, chi2 0.40 on 1, against ul/e_phenb10_xzzx_X_d7_p0.03_corr_21.txt): 0.81(4); 4.8, 4.7; delta* 0.078. Delta-dependent.
  - hw_tr 3% L_Y (cons/x3_Y_a.txt and cons/x3_Y_b.txt against cons/z3_X.txt): 0.68(8); 3.3, 3.3; delta* 0.075. hw_tr 6% at 195 qubits L_Y (litrev/hwtr_xyz2_Y_d7.txt and litrev/hwtr_xyz2_Y_d7b.txt against XZZX interpolated between d = 9 and 11): 0.54(10); 3.3, 3.3; delta* 0.126. phen_b10 18/16 against XZZX d = 4 (bq/p03.log): 0.70(5); 5.3, 3.1; delta* 0.097. All three are delta-dependent.
  - Ties, failing (b):
    - point A (p_T 4%, 0.3% gates, 1% readout, f = 0; hwrev_q7/A_xyz2_X.txt, 174 errors, against hwrev_q7/A_xzzx_X.txt): 0.75(6); 3.7, 2.2.
    - hw_tr p_T 4%, 99/97 qubits, r = 3d (litrev/hwtr4_xyz2_X.txt, 62 errors): 0.61(8); 3.9, 2.3.
    - m1 X, 4 runs, 258 errors: 0.70(4), or 0.70(7) with f = 1.66; 5.7, 2.0 (t = 3.43 on 3 dof; a per-run t-test gives 3.28, also 2.0 sigma). Without cons/m1_x_X_b.txt: 0.77(5); 3.8, 3.8; delta* 0.096, delta-dependent.
    - phen_b10 2% L_X, 10 runs, 473 errors: 0.78(4), or 0.78(6) with f = 1.53; 5.3, 2.7 (t = 3.45 on 9 dof; a per-run t-test gives 3.89, 2.9 sigma).
- Qubit-matched losses:
  - phen 98/100 (bq/phen.log, 243 against 518 errors): 2.36(18); 11.0, 8.7; delta* 0.39 (z 3.1 at delta 0.37). Holds.
  - biased10, 99/97, p = 3e-3, r = 3d, L_Y (C32; 11 BM runs in ul/g_biased10_xyz2_Y_*, stat/runb10_xyz2_Y_bm_*, bq/b10.log and ovc/resb10.jsonl, 150 errors, chi2 4.20 on 10, against XZZX X corr pooled over 3 runs, 7,868 errors): 3.35(28); 14.7, 14.7; delta* 1.3. Holds.
  - hw_rr, p = 4%, 99/97, compared by per-run p_L as in C20. XYZ^2 corr_gauge (rv/rr2_xyz2_Y_corr_gauge.txt, 33,044 errors) against XZZX corr (rv/rr2_xzzx_X_corr.txt, 14,883 errors): 2.10(2); 75, 44. MWPM on both sides (rv/rr_xyz2_Y.txt, 70,997 errors, against rv/rr_xzzx_X.txt, 27,593): 2.09(1); 104, 61. Both are outside (c) and hold. BM, XYZ^2's best decoder here (rv/rr2_xyz2_Y_bm.txt, 887 errors): 1.98(7); 19.8, 11.6; delta* 0.225. Delta-dependent.
  - phen 50/49 (bq/phen.log, 416 against 468 errors): 1.83(12); 8.9, 5.3; delta* 0.189. Delta-dependent.
  - Run E (C37; hwrev_q7/E_xyz2_Y.txt and hwrev_q7/E2_xyz2_Y.txt, 112 errors, chi2 0.01 on 1, against hwrev_q7/E_xzzx_X.txt, 11,601 errors): 1.72(16); 5.7, 5.7; delta* 0.217. Delta-dependent.
  - phen_b10 q = 0, 50/49, 3%, L_Y (cons/cc_phen0_Y.txt and bq/cc4.log, 416 errors, chi2 1.98 on 3, against XZZX X corr in bq/cc4.log, 759 errors): 1.44(9); 6.0, 4.7; delta* 0.213. Delta-dependent.
  - phen 18/16 (bq/phen.log, XYZ^2 Y 592 errors against XZZX Z corr 579): 1.36(8); 5.3, 3.1; delta* 0.085. Delta-dependent.

claims.regime: Literature cross-check of the campaign's competitors and of the published case for XYZ^2
claims.statement:
Literature, consistent with the campaign at circuit level, with these qualifications.

1. Hetenyi-Wootton (2306.17786).
- Combining their Table I corners with their rule 1/p_ic = 1/p_G + 1/p_T + 1/p_RR ranks XYZ^2 (0.41%) above XZZX (0.35%). That combination is derived here. The paper prints only the surface code's 0.65% and XZZX's 0.35%. Their readout corner puts XYZ^2 first (16.5 vs 14.5, about 1 sigma of their fit deviations). Neither is reproduced as an advantage here (C19, C20).
- The rotated (0.65%) and 3-CX (0.53%, derived the same way) surface codes beat XYZ^2 on that combination.
- Their slow-readout scenario names XZZX.
- They expect eta_T of order 10 for spins, and call real-time decoding a requirement.
- Their XYZ^2 uses ZZ links, a square lattice, and two readout rounds per cycle.

2. 2112.06036.
- Its equal-data-qubit advantage is code capacity at eta = 10 with near-ML (EWD) decoding, against XZZX in its distance-d frame. Reading its Fig. 7a inset: about 1.7x at p = 0.22 to 2.7x at 0.16, at 121 data qubits.
- Against the d^2 frame (Fig. 7c) it is near parity, 1.00-1.16x. Treating that as parity with a best-framed square surface code is this document's inference; the paper says only that failure 'scales with the number of data qubits'.
- At the paper's bias, eta = 10, the campaign's closest analogue was run at one point only, p_T = 3%, the lowest p_T tested, and shows no significant edge there. In hw_tr (perfect syndromes, dephasing during readout and reset) at p_T = 3%, 99 vs 97 qubits, r = 3d, XYZ^2 with BM gives 9.75(98)e-5 per round in its weaker basis against 1.208(14)e-4 for the d-frame XZZX with corr. The ratio is 0.81(8), 2.4 sigma, stat only: a tie with the only competitor run at eta = 10. At eta = 20 and the same p_T the ratio is 0.68(8), stat only. That is the weakest of the three eta = 20 p_T points and 1.1 sigma from the eta = 10 value, so these data do not separate a bias effect from a p_T effect (inference). Whether eta = 10 shows the edge at p_T = 4-6%, where the eta = 20 ratio is 0.61(4)-0.61(8), is untested. Both 2112.06036 (Fig. 7a, p = 0.16-0.22) and 2505.03691 place the published advantage near threshold.
- At eta = 20 the hw_tr edge (C35) holds against every tested competitor, stat only, but only the d-frame XZZX is decoded well enough to count. The d^2-frame proxies do worse than the d-frame XZZX, the opposite of the code-level effect, so they measure decoder failure, not the frame (inference). At p_T = 4%, Y-biased XZZX gives 9.03(52)e-4 per round with BM and 2.581(10)e-3 with corr, the d-frame XZZX 3.050(28)e-4 with corr, and XYZ^2 1.86(24)e-4 with BM. At p_T = 6%, Z-biased XY gives 3.51(12)e-3 to 3.69(12)e-3 with BM, XZZX 1.089(6)e-3 with corr, and XYZ^2 6.68(45)e-4 with BM. An ML or tensor-network d^2-frame competitor under hw_tr is untested; at code level (Fig. 7c) it is near parity.
- XYZ^2's ML (MPS) threshold at eta = 10, 28.61(5)% (2505.03691), matches the XY code's tensor-network threshold, 28.2(2)% (1708.08474; 28.1(2)% in 1812.08186), within 2.0-2.5 sigma of the published errors. 2112.06036 puts XYZ^2 and XZZX both at 'about 28%'.
- The paper hoped the weight-2 links would offset the weight-6 cost, and flagged measurement noise on the weight-6 checks as a risk. At threshold level the gap diagnostic does not support that particular risk: with noiseless links and no idling, XYZ^2 ties XZZX (ratio 1.01(3)). The measured threshold-level cost is idling (0.60(1) of the gap) and link noise (0.23(2)). With noiseless links but idling kept, XYZ^2 reaches 0.77(2) of XZZX. In a d = 7/9 MWPM schedule-search diagnostic (C22), removing only the gate-layer idling, where link ancillas wait in 4 of the 6 layers and data qubits in 2, raises XYZ^2's SD6 crossing from 0.38(2)% to 0.57(4)%, against 0.65(2)% with all idling removed. Gate-layer idling is thus about 0.70(16) of the idle gain at MWPM. Below threshold the weight-6 map costs qubits per distance (C4).

3. 2505.03691 (same group) calls the thresholds 'competitive' (abstract) and describes the advantage over XZZX as holding 'close to the threshold'.

Competitor baselines:
- XZZX MWPM SD6 0.697(9)% vs 0.66% (2505.17718).
- Honeycomb em3 1.976(20)% vs 1.5-2.0%.
- Our SD6 honeycomb, 0.218(3)%, is at the bottom of the published 0.2-0.357% range, so wins over the honeycomb are inflated.

Decoders:
- A re-implementation of 2505.03691's sequential matching decoder (seq_hard, with the paper's time boundaries) crosses at 3.17(9)% (X) and 3.23(10)% (Y) at eta = 0.5, and at 3.55(6)% and 3.41(13)% at eta = 10, for d = 5/7. The paper gives 3.42(1)% and 3.49(2)%. That matches at eta = 10 and is 0.19-0.25 pp low at eta = 0.5 (1.9-2.8 sigma, stat only).
- The campaign's own sequential decoder (seq_match) gives higher r = d fits over d = 11-21. For phen they are 3.636(49)-3.644(39)%, 6.3-6.5% above 3.42(1)% and 3.0-5.6 sigma (fit stat plus syst, combined with the published error). For phen_b10 they are 3.584(59)-3.682(81)%, 2.7-5.5% above 3.49(2)% and 1.5-4.1 sigma on the same basis. Whether the excess comes from the decoder variant, the frame-start time boundaries or finite-size drift is untested. It does not indicate weaker decoding.
- Our BP decoders exceed every published XYZ^2 decoder there (phen_b10 5.54(5)% in the weaker basis against 4.30(2)% for their belief-matching).
- In hw_tr, the comparison of XYZ^2's MWPM crossing with published code-capacity values is not like-for-like (C21).

claims.regime: hw_tr: noiseless gates, readout and reset (perfect syndromes); Z-biased Pauli dephasing (eta = 20) on data qubits only while ancillas are reset and read out (p_T per round). This is Hetenyi-Wootton's idling placement, with no gate-layer idling. XX links; both-basis memory; MDR time boundaries; equal total qubits (4d^2-1 vs 2d^2-1); r = 3d plus one r = 6d point; XYZ^2 BM vs square XZZX corr. Pilots in docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/{litrev,cons,hwrev_q7,litlens}
claims.statement:
Measured in pilots, for memory. Ratios are XYZ^2's error per round over XZZX's, with Poisson errors. All errors are stat only. Significance follows C33: z = |ln R|/sigma under three error models, the same whichever code leads. (a) Poisson. (b) Shot-level scaling, sigma^2 = f1^2/N1 + f2^2/N2: f = max(1, sqrt(chi2/dof)) from a pool's own replicates, f = 1.7 for any single run on either side, and a Student t conversion when f > 1 is estimated. (c) An extra log-rate variance delta^2 per XYZ^2 BM run, with runs pooled by inverse variance. z is listed as (a), (b), (c) at delta = 0.15/0.25. delta* is the largest delta at which (c) still gives 3. Labels follow C33. A lead or loss holds when (a) and (b) give 3 or more and delta* is at least 0.37, the top of C33's bracket of 0.065-0.37. A point that passes (a) and (b) with a smaller delta* is delta-dependent and is not counted. A point that fails (a) or (b) is a tie.

With BM decoding, XYZ^2 has a nominally lower error per round than square XZZX in its distance-d frame at every eta = 20 point in this regime. One lead holds under C33's rule. It is r = 6d at 99/97 qubits and p_T 4%, worse basis against worse basis, 0.384(39): z 9.5, 9.4, 6.5/4.7, delta* 0.43. XYZ^2's L_X against the same XZZX L_X gives 0.362(38), delta* 0.46. Every r = 3d lead is a tie or delta-dependent. Together with phen_b10 (C31), hw_tr is one of two idealized models with a nominal memory edge, and neither models a device.

The r = 6d lead rests on three conditions:
- Its delta* is only 15-22% above the bracket top of 0.374. That top comes from one flagged replicate set with one degree of freedom (cons/x3_X_a.txt and cons/x3_X_b.txt; C33).
- Model (c) treats the two XYZ^2 runs per basis (cons/b_x_Y_a.txt and cons/b_x_Y_b.txt; cons/b_x_X_a.txt and cons/b_x_X_b.txt; a/b runs of cons/hwtr_r.py, seeded from time and pid) as having independent offsets. If each pair shared one offset, delta* would be 0.30 (L_Y) and 0.32 (L_X), below 0.37, and the lead would be delta-dependent. Two of C33's four flagged excesses lie inside a/b pairs of this kind (cons/x3_X_a/b and cons/m1_x_X_a/b), which supports per-run offsets (inference).
- It is measured against XZZX's weaker basis. Better basis against better basis (XYZ^2 L_X against XZZX L_Z, cons/b_z_Z.txt) gives 0.564(59), which is delta-dependent (below).

The number of established results depends on delta. At C33's lower estimate, delta 0.065-0.074 from statrev/homog.py, five more leads would hold. Three are worse-basis leads: r = 3d at p_T 6% (delta* 0.148), p_T 3% L_Y (0.075, only marginally) and 195 qubits (0.125). Two are better-basis leads: r = 6d (0.227) and m1 (0.100). Two losses would also hold: run E (0.217) and the boundary check below (0.213). The rule discounts leads and losses alike.

It is not a use case, for four reasons:
- It holds for memory only. For r = 1 MDR preparation, the paper's subject, in the same model (p_T 4%, eta 20, 99/97 qubits), XYZ^2 is 16.8(11)-18.5(7)x worse in L_X and 23.4(13)x worse weaker basis against weaker basis. The archived runs docs/data/campaign/usefulness_pilots/r1_xyz2.out and r1_xzzx.out (script r1.py) give XYZ^2 d = 5 depth6 L_X 9.309(21)e-4 with corr_gauge (1952 errors) against XZZX d = 7 L_X 5.021(15)e-5 with corr (1053 errors). That is 18.5(7)x: z 76, 45, outside (c). Unarchived repeats with the same script add BM runs: depth6 L_X 9.52(51)e-4 and 9.50(73)e-4, and with the both schedule L_X 8.95(52)e-4 and L_Y 1.245(60)e-3, against XZZX L_X 5.32(16)e-5 and 5.47(16)e-5. These BM losses give z 10.8 or more under (c) at delta 0.25 and delta* 0.94 or more. The loss holds. The phen_b10 edge also reverses at r = 1: 8.4(6)x (usefulness_pilots/r1_phen_xyz2.out and r1_phen_xzzx.out; C31).
- Three decoders were run on XYZ^2 under hw_tr: BM, corr_gauge and MWPM. Only BM gives the memory lead. With corr_gauge and MWPM it is a loss at the one point probed (below). The MWPM pair crossings at r = d (docs/data/campaign/hw/diag_hw_tr_centers.csv, d = 7/9, fit errors) also put XYZ^2 nominally below XZZX: XYZ^2 X 10.49(55)% against XZZX Z 18.95(160)%, 5.0 sigma stat only and 1.7 sigma with the 5/7 to 7/9 shift as syst, a tie (C21). XYZ^2 Y is 13.99(166)%, and XZZX X has no crossing up to 44%. The other eleven decoders in scripts/run_decoder_threshold_sweep.py (lines 85-105) were not run under hw_tr: corr_links, seq_soft, seq_erasure, seq_match, bp_full, bp_corr, tesseract, cfe, cfe0, tnml and cfe_tn. Whether they widen or remove the edge is untested.
- The model leaves out gate-layer idling. There XYZ^2 has 4.9x the exposure (254 vs 52 sites per round). In the m1 mixture, putting back 2% of that idling gives 1.02(7), so no edge is seen (C37).
- At the readout time that Hetenyi-Wootton find QEC-optimal for the rotated surface code on their example device (5.8 us; run E of C37, C38), XYZ^2 is 1.72(16)x worse: z 5.7, 5.7, 3.8/2.7, delta* 0.22. That is a delta-dependent loss. XYZ^2's own optimal readout time is untested.

Weaker basis, XYZ^2 BM against XZZX corr. XZZX BM equals XZZX corr within errors where both were run: 0.99(6) at p_T 6% and 1.08(12) in m1. Elsewhere only XZZX corr exists.
- 99/97 qubits, r = 3d:
  - p_T 6%: 0.613(42); 7.2, 4.2, 3.0/1.9; delta* 0.148. Delta-dependent.
  - p_T 4%: 0.608(77); 3.9, 2.3, 2.5/1.8. A tie.
  - p_T 3%: 0.679(80); 3.3, 3.3, 2.45/1.8; delta* 0.075. Delta-dependent.
- 195 qubits, p_T 6%: 0.538(100) against XZZX log-interpolated between d = 9 and 11; 3.3, 3.3, 2.9/2.4; delta* 0.125. Delta-dependent. XZZX d = 11, with 24% more qubits, ties (1.06(20)). Nominally, XYZ^2 at 195 qubits matches XZZX interpolated to 237(13) qubits, 0.82(4) of XZZX's qubit count, with Poisson errors only.
- r = 6d (99/97, p_T 4%): 0.384(39), the lead above. L_Y alone is 0.40(6) at r = 3d and 0.38(4) at r = 6d. The worse-basis gain at r = 6d comes from L_X's time-boundary term (C9).
- Size trend: Lambda is 6.5(13) against the break-even 5.5-5.8. The difference is 0.5-0.8 sigma, so it is unresolved.
- m1 mixture (p_T 4% plus 0.1% gate and 1% readout error; no reset, single-qubit or gate-layer idle noise): at 99/97 the ratio is 0.700(44); 5.7, 2.0 (f = 1.66 from four replicates, t 3.4 on 3 dof), 3.6/2.5. A tie, because it fails (b). At 195 it is 0.81(17), a tie. The erosion projection, Lambda 2.95(64) against 3.3-3.4, differs by 0.5-0.7 sigma and is unresolved.

Boundary sensitivity (C9). phen q = 0 at eta = 10, p = 3%, 50/49 data qubits also has perfect syndromes, but it puts a full noise layer before the first round. There XYZ^2's L_Y is 2.00e-4 (416 errors), 2.05x its hw_tr eta = 10 value, while XZZX rises 14.5%. The hw_tr tie 0.81(8) becomes 1.445(88); 6.0, 4.7, 3.8/2.6; delta* 0.21. That is a delta-dependent loss. No such check exists at eta = 20, so whether the eta = 20 edge survives a harsher preparation boundary is untested.

Decoder dependence, at p_T 4%, 99/97, r = 3d:
- XYZ^2 corr_gauge, worse basis, 6.927e-4 (usefulness_pilots/cg_Y.txt, 10,873 errors) against XZZX corr 3.050e-4 (litrev/hwtr4_xzzx_X.txt): 2.27(3)x worse.
- XYZ^2 MWPM, from unarchived runs of usefulness_pilots/rv/eqprobe.py, 4.58e-3 to 4.61e-3 against the same XZZX value: 15x worse.
This repository's Python BM takes 0.33-0.36 s per shot for XYZ^2 at d = 11. At d = 5, r = 15 it takes 0.017-0.025 s per shot, about 1.1-1.7 ms per round. These times were measured on SD6 graphs and are indicative for hw_tr. Whether an optimized BP-class decoder can run in real time is untested.

Bias, worse basis, at p_T 3%, the only p_T run at eta = 10 and 100. eta = 10 gives 0.807(82) (z 2.1, a tie). eta = 20 gives 0.679(80) (delta-dependent, above). eta = 100 gives 1.14(19) (a tie). The differences from eta = 20 are 1.1 and 2.5 sigma (Poisson), so the bias window is not established. In the better basis at eta = 100, XYZ^2 X is 4.19e-5 against XZZX Z 1.74e-5. The ratio is 2.41(45); 4.7, 2.75, 3.7/2.8. That nominal reversal is a tie, because it fails (b). No growth of the edge with bias is seen, although the 2d^2 pure-Z distance would predict one. BM may limit it (inference).

Competitors:
- XY (BM, 6%) is 5.2(4)-5.5(4)x worse than XYZ^2, and square XZZX under Y-biased idling (BM, 4%) is 4.9(7)x worse. Each is the d^2-frame code for its bias, yet each comes out worse than d-frame XZZX: XY by 3.2(1)-3.4(1)x at 6%, and Y-biased XZZX by 3.0(2)x with BM and 8.5(1)x with corr at 4%. 2112.06036 finds the opposite at code level (XZZX failure suppressed under Y bias), so these runs measure decoder failure, not the frame (inference). The edge against a d^2-frame competitor, with a decoder that exploits that frame, is untested.
- CSS and the honeycomb were never run at equal qubits. Under hw_tr with MWPM at r = d, CSS Z has no crossing up to 44% (measured, threshold level only; docs/data/campaign/hw/diag_hw_tr_centers.csv), because the CSS Z logical fails only through the weak X and Y parts of the channel. For preparing |0>, a CSS patch would therefore likely win at equal qubits (inference).
- Rectangular, co-prime or ML-decoded surface patches were not run. Syndromes are perfect, so per-round code-capacity decoding applies, and 2112.06036 Fig. 7c shows near parity against the d^2 frame.

hw_tr is the closest analogue in the repo of the 2112.06036 code-capacity regime. That paper's bias, eta = 10, was run under hw_tr only at p_T 3%. That is the lowest p_T tested, and there the eta = 20 lead is also weakest. The ratio there is 0.81(8), a tie. claims.regime: Platform map: which device classes the campaign models represent, and whether they can host XYZ^2's circuit
claims.statement:
Inference from the model definitions, combined with measured results (pilots where marked). Error ratios are XYZ^2/competitor (above 1 means XYZ^2 is worse). Pilot errors are stat only. Pilot significances follow C33: z = |ln R|/sigma under three error models. (a) is Poisson. (b) multiplies each run's Poisson error by f. A pool takes f = max(1, sqrt(chi2/dof)) from its own replicates, read as Student t when f > 1 is estimated, and a single run takes f = 1.7. (c) adds a run-level log-rate variance delta^2 to each XYZ^2 BM run, and delta* is the largest delta at which (c) still gives z = 3. A pilot lead or loss holds if z is at least 3 under (a) and (b) and delta* is at least 0.37. A pilot without XYZ^2 BM runs is outside (c) and holds on (a) and (b). One that passes (a) and (b) with a smaller delta* is delta-dependent and is not counted. One that fails (a) or (b) is a tie.

Scope of the verdict. No modelled platform gives XYZ^2 an established use.
- r = 1 preparation: no tested fixed-footprint window remains under SI1000. On 35 qubits a CSS patch beats XYZ^2 d = 3 in each basis (pilots, below). In the idealized spin corner hw_tr (p_T 4%, eta = 20, 99/97 qubits), r = 1 preparation is a measured loss. XYZ^2 d = 5 depth6 L_X with corr_gauge gives 9.31(21)e-4, against 5.02(15)e-5 for XZZX d = 7 X with corr: 18.5(7)x worse, z 76 under (a) and 45 under (b), outside (c) (pilot, stat only). Repeats with other decoders, schedules and bases are also losses of more than an order of magnitude (C9, C35).
- Memory: one idealized window is not closed by measurement. With spin-like idling only during readout and reset (hw_tr) and no gate-layer dephasing (f = 0), XYZ^2 with BM leads XZZX, the best competitor run (C35). With small gate and readout errors added, the lead is not established (m1, below). The example spin device is unlikely to meet these conditions (inference, below). The window is for memory only: r = 1 preparation in the same model loses (above).

Ions:
- These are the only models calibrated to real devices that natively host the circuit (all-to-all connectivity).
- At both device points a surface patch that fits prepares the state better: 2.8-37.3x at Helios and 4.7-26.5x at H2 (C11).
- In docs/data/campaign/competitors_table.csv, XYZ^2's threshold is nominally below the best competitor in every ion row but one (ratios 0.115-0.833). The exception, h2_p at r = 5 (ratio 1.41), is a Tesseract fit of L_X only: 0.817(17)% (stat only), with nu at the 6.0 fit bound and chi2 14.8 on 7 points. It sits under a crosstalk model whose listed thresholds are fit artifacts for every code (C13, C27).
- Ion memory error is pure Z, about 5-6e-3 per data qubit per round at d = 5 (Helios 6.3e-3, H2 5.25e-3). It is applied in every gate layer and every measurement step. That is hw_t's placement, where XYZ^2 loses (threshold 0.13 of XZZX), not hw_tr's.

Superconducting:
- Only SI1000 and its repeated-link variant are superconducting-inspired.
- SI1000, r = 1, p = 1e-3, 35 qubits (pilots). XYZ^2 d = 3 prepares its MDR basis L_X with error 1.139(33)e-3 (corr_gauge) and 1.1698(21)e-3 (MWPM). A 6x3 CSS patch on 35 qubits, built with the repository's competitor circuit, schedule and noise, has X-basis fault distance 6 and error 6.39(16)e-5 (corr). XYZ^2 is 17.8x (corr_gauge) and 18.3x (MWPM) worse: z 74 and 113 under (a), 44 and 66 under (b), outside (c). XYZ^2 BM (1.170(58)e-3) is 18.3x worse, z 52 and 31, delta* 0.97, so that loss also holds. In the other basis, XYZ^2's best L_Y (2.773(73)e-3, both schedule, corr_gauge) is 1.53-1.62x the square CSS D = 4 patch on 31 qubits (1.715(40)e-3 to 1.8117(29)e-3): z 12.5-18.2 under (a) and 7.3-10.7 under (b), outside (c). Both patches fit every footprint from 35 to 48 qubits, so no window remains there.
- Each basis needs its own patch. The 6x3 patch's Z basis (fault distance 3) has error 4.90(10)e-3, 1.77x XYZ^2's best L_Y.
- Square patches alone leave a granularity gap. Against CSS and XZZX D = 4 on 31 qubits, XYZ^2's L_X is 0.60-0.70x. Against the lowest square-patch value (CSS-Z corr, 1.715(40)e-3), corr_gauge gives 0.664(25), z 11.0 under (a) and 6.5 under (b), outside (c), so this lead over square patches holds. BM gives 0.682(37), z 7.0 and 4.1 with delta* 0.12, which is delta-dependent (C11).
- The repo's degree-6 circuit would need routing on degree-4 or heavy-hex chips. Routing was not modelled, which favours XYZ^2.
- Hetenyi-Wootton's square-lattice layout (ancilla pairs, links read in a second readout round) avoids degree 6 at the cost of a second readout window.
- 2109.13308 runs a related code on heavy-hex with an auxiliary qubit per link. It has no threshold study.

Spin arrays:
- XYZ^2 loses wherever idling is charged in every gate layer (hw_t, threshold 0.13 of XZZX). It also loses the readout-only corner below threshold (hw_rr, C20).
- Hetenyi-Wootton's idling placement (hw_tr) plus gate and readout error, f = 0. XYZ^2 BM against XZZX corr, 99/97 qubits, r = 3d, eta = 20 (pilots). Values are R (Poisson error), then z under (a) and (b), then delta* where (a) and (b) pass:
  - m1 (pG 0.1%, p_R 1%, p_T 4%; four replicates): 0.70(4); 5.7, 2.0 (f 1.66, t 3.4 on 3 dof). A tie: it fails (b).
  - A (pG 0.3%, p_R 1%, p_T 4%; one run): 0.75(6); 3.7, 2.2. A tie: it fails (b).
  - E (pG 0.1%, p_R 2.7%, p_T 1.5%; the 5.8 us readout that Hetenyi-Wootton find QEC-optimal for the rotated surface code): 1.72(16); 5.7, 5.7; delta* 0.22. Its two replicates are Poisson-consistent (chi2 0.01 on 1 dof), so (b) applies no scale to the XYZ^2 pool. It is delta-dependent: a loss for run offsets up to delta 0.22, not counted at the top of the bracket (0.37).
  - XYZ^2's best tested value (1.13e-3 per round, at E) is 1.72(16)x XZZX's best (6.60e-4, at E). Each code's own optimal readout time is untested, so this compares tested operating points on one example device (C37, C38).
  - E has no reset error. The device's combined readout-and-reset error at 5.8 us is 3.1% (Eq. 8, p_res 0.5%), against the 2.7% modelled. Its effect on the ratio is untested.
- The f = 0 lead depends on conditions the example device is unlikely to meet:
  - No gate-layer dephasing. At f = 0.02 (0.08% per idle site) the m1 ratio is 1.02(7) (Poisson), a tie. 0 < f < 0.02 is untested. The device's f is not pinned down (inference). Neither the repository nor 2306.17786 gives gate durations. For an assumed 100 ns gate layer:
    - Treated as its own idle phase, as Hetenyi-Wootton treat idle phases (App. D, Eq. D1), the layer gives f of about 6e-5 to 7e-4. The low end is literal Eqs. 3-4, whose sum is the Gaussian term alone, 2.0e-6 per site. The high end adds Eq. 3's T1 term (0.8-1.2e-5) to the Gaussian term without Eq. 4's subtraction, which makes p_T2 negative at 100 ns.
    - Added to the readout window's dephasing, the layer gives f of 0.0078 (linear in time) to 0.015 (Gaussian, Eq. 12) at the 9.8 us readout, and 0.011 to 0.022 at the 5.8 us readout. f then grows with layer duration and reaches 0.02 at 130-260 ns (9.8 us) or 90-180 ns (5.8 us).
    - The device's f can therefore lie anywhere from near 0 to above 0.02.
  - eta = 20. At p_T 3%, eta = 20 gives 0.68(8), eta = 10 gives 0.81(8) and eta = 100 gives 1.14(19) (Poisson). eta = 10 and eta = 20 differ by 1.1 sigma, so the bias dependence is not established. With T2 = 50 us, Eq. 5 puts eta = 20 at a data T1 of about 2.0-3.0 ms at the device's 9.8 and 5.8 us readout times (inference).
  - One readout window per cycle and XX links.
  - BM decoding. BM takes 17-25 CPU ms per 15-round d = 5 shot (SD6 timing), or 1.1-1.7 ms per round, against a cycle of about 9-13 us. Whether a BP-class decoder can run in real time is untested.
- Spin-blockade readout uses ancilla pairs. XYZ^2 therefore needs either two readout windows per cycle (their 4d^2 layout, ZZ links) or about 6d^2 qubits for one window (inference). Changing the link orientation changes the ancilla basis change (Hadamards on ancillas); it adds no data-side gates.
- Shuttling architectures (2601.10461) apply dephasing per two-qubit gate to the shuttled qubits. That is the biased-gate placement, where XYZ^2 loses (C5, C6), not hw_t's per-idle-site charge. At equal qubits the two codes have nearly equal two-qubit gate counts (170 vs 168 at 99/97; C11).

Other:
- Pair measurements have been demonstrated in small circuit-QED devices and are targeted by Majorana tetrons. The honeycomb code is native there, and its threshold is 6.1x XYZ^2's (C14).
- Cat qubits deploy repetition codes. The biased models cover their bias range, and XYZ^2 loses there.
- Neutral atoms were not modelled. Atom loss is a dominant error source there (2603.24237). Under erasure the literature finds XZZX leading or tied with CSS. sd6_noidle is not a proxy for them.
- phen, phen_b10, sd6_il, hw_tr and the gap variants are not hardware models.
